Every entry names the production source the code comes from, because these are product
contracts (route bodies, CLI exit codes), not harness inventions.
exit 1 = the command could not run, exit 2 = it ran and found the input wrong.
stderr carries {code, reason, path?, detail?}; stdout is the result document.

body.message: This registry does not authorize the requested map.

comment: Two distinct transfer faults with the same required outcome: nothing installed and no
promoted partial. The truncated case aborts mid-body; the corrupt case serves complete
bytes that do not match the advertised digest.
A cache root that cannot hold the corpus must be refused with the path in the message.
A regular file used as a parent directory gives a deterministic ENOTDIR on every OS and
for every uid, unlike a chmod-based read-only directory which root ignores.
The control token is a per-start secret. Production code states it never appears in a URL,
browser history or referrer, and that the session cookie value is derived from it rather
than being it. These are the assertions that hold that line.
The decoy below is a synthetic, non-production value; no real credential belongs in E2E.
